flashcard_questions.q: Which event drove mass Irish migration to Liverpool between 1846 and 1852?
How many Irish people moved to Liverpool during the famine?
Which area of Liverpool did Irish migrants mainly settle in?
When did the Chinese community in Liverpool begin?
Which Liverpool district became home to the oldest Afro-Caribbean community in Europe?

flashcard_questions.a: Transporting cargo in standard containers moved between ships, trains and trucks without unloading.

flashcard_questions.q: Why did trade move away from Liverpool's docks?
flashcard_questions.a: The docks were too shallow for the larger container ships.

flashcard_questions.q: How many homes were destroyed in Liverpool's May Blitz of 1941?
When did the Liverpool Overhead Railway close permanently?
How high did unemployment in Liverpool rise during the 1980s?
How many people left Liverpool each year during the 1980s?
What was Liverpool's peak population in 1931?
How many police officers were injured in the 1981 riots in Liverpool?
What is the negative multiplier effect?
flashcard_questions.a: A downward spiral where job losses lead to less spending and further decline.

notes: 15 cards: 2 term-to-definition (containerisation, negative multiplier effect), 11 case-study-to-fact naming Liverpool or the district with one figure or date each (1.3 million Irish, Scotland Road, 1834, Toxteth, 10,000 homes, 1956, 20% unemployment, 12,000 leaving, 850,000, 485,000, 450 officers), 1 event card (Irish Potato Famine), 1 cause-to-consequence (shallow docks). The 90,000 Irish-born residents of 1851, the 50% Irish ancestry share, the Blue Funnel line, the Chinatown streets, the 184 damaged dock berths and the Tate & Lyle closure were trimmed to stay within 15.
